evals.name: client-process-map-with-numbers
evals.prompt: We have a workshop next week with our client Northwind (they make logistics software). Draw their current incident-to-fix process as a clean Excalidraw diagram: support ticket in Zendesk, triage by L2, Jira bug, sprint planning, dev, peer review, QA on staging, merge, release train every 3 weeks, then deployment to customers (takes weeks, nobody measures it). We measured over 9 months: median 2.1 working days from Jira creation to dev start, dev 1.5 days median, review 0.8 days, QA 0.6 days, waiting for the release train 12 calendar days median. In the workshop they also said about 30% of bugs get reopened, but we have not measured that. Give me a .excalidraw file I can open.
evals.expected_output: A generator script and a .excalidraw process map, left to right, readable in 30 seconds: figures with unit and statistic, the 30% marked as said not measured, deployment shown as not measured, a small author/client box, a legend, sources in a footer, no lint errors.
expectations: A .excalidraw file and the Python script that generates it are both delivered
Durations distinguish working days from calendar days
The 30% reopen figure is marked as said / not measured, or placed in an open-questions box, not shown as a measured fact
Deployment to customers is visibly marked as not measured (dashed or labelled)
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors on the delivered file
No box contains more than 40 words

evals.name: casual-architecture-poster-fr
evals.prompt: fais-moi un beau schéma excalidraw de notre pipeline data : postgres et s3 en sources, airbyte pour l'ingestion, dbt dans snowflake, metabase pour les dashboards. c'est pour montrer au CTO demain, pas trop verbeux stp
evals.expected_output: A sparse architecture poster in French: columns sources → ingestion → warehouse → consumers, one short line per component, a one-sentence message, no invented metrics, generated by a script, lint clean.
expectations: The diagram shows the flow sources → Airbyte → dbt/Snowflake → Metabase left to right
No box contains more than 40 words
No numeric metric is invented (no throughput, latency or volume figures that the user did not give)
Text on the canvas is in French
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors on the delivered file

evals.name: hand-drawn-concept-explainer
evals.prompt: I'm writing a blog post explaining retrieval-augmented generation to non-technical readers. Can you make a friendly, hand-drawn style Excalidraw diagram of how a question gets answered: the question, searching the company documents, picking the most relevant passages, giving them to the language model with the question, and the answer with sources. Keep it simple and warm, not corporate.
evals.expected_output: A hand-drawn style (Excalifont, roughness 1) explainer with five steps in a clear reading order, plain-language labels, very few words, one accent colour for the key idea, no jargon beyond what the user used, lint clean.
expectations: Text elements use the hand-drawn font (fontFamily 5) and shapes use roughness 1
The five steps appear in reading order: question, search documents, pick passages, give to the model, answer with sources
No box contains more than 25 words
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors on the delivered file

evals.name: as-is-and-target-shared-grid
evals.prompt: Here's our current code review process: the dev opens a PR, it waits for a senior reviewer (median 1.8 working days of waiting), the senior reviews, the dev fixes, then merge. The target we want to propose: a bot pass runs first on every PR, and the senior gate only applies to PRs touching payments. Make the current and the target as two Excalidraw diagrams that can be compared side by side. Keep our terms 'senior gate' and 'bot pass' exactly as they are.
evals.expected_output: Two .excalidraw files sharing layout constants so shared steps align, 'senior gate' and 'bot pass' verbatim, a legend for proposed vs current, the 1.8 working-day median in the current diagram, a separate path for payment PRs in the target.
expectations: Two .excalidraw files are delivered, one for the current process and one for the target
Shared steps have the same x position in both files
The exact strings 'senior gate' and 'bot pass' appear in the target diagram
A legend states which colour means proposed and which means current
The target shows a separate path for PRs touching payments

evals.name: non-additive-medians-trap
evals.prompt: Can you make an excalidraw of our ticket lead time? Per step medians: 3 days before dev, 5 days dev+review, 2 days waiting for deploy. The median total is 14 days. Make the bar look proportional.
evals.expected_output: A diagram that does not imply 3 + 5 + 2 = 14: it shows the 14-day total with a caption that step medians do not add up, or flags the gap explicitly; units and statistics labelled.
expectations: The diagram does not present the three step medians as segments summing to the 14-day total without a caveat
A caption or note explains that step medians do not add up to the total median

evals.name: wrong-owner-slide-deck
evals.prompt: Create a 10-slide pitch deck about our Q3 results for the board, with charts of revenue and churn.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not take over: a slide deck with numeric charts belongs to deck or charting tooling. At most it offers to draw one supporting diagram.
expectations: No Excalidraw diagram is produced as the main deliverable
The response routes the request to slide or chart tooling

evals.name: sober-board-explainer
evals.prompt: Our board wants to understand how our new fraud check works before approving it. Four steps: the payment comes in, we score it against known patterns, risky ones go to a human analyst, the customer gets an answer within a minute. Make me an Excalidraw I can put in the board pack. Keep it serious.
evals.expected_output: A sober style (corporate or editorial): neutral cards, one accent on the step that matters, no per-step pastel colours, no cartoon faces, the user's four steps in order, lint clean.
expectations: The diagram does not give each step its own colour (at most one accent family plus neutrals)
The four steps appear in order
No figure other than 'within a minute' is shown
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors on the delivered file

evals.name: black-and-white-print
evals.prompt: I need to print our onboarding checklist flow on a black-and-white printer for new hires: laptop setup, accounts, first pairing session, first small ticket, demo on Friday. Excalidraw please.
evals.expected_output: The mono style: only black, white and greys; emphasis by weight, fill or dashes; readable when printed.
expectations: Every stroke and fill colour on the canvas is a grey (R = G = B)
The five steps appear in order
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors on the delivered file

evals.name: dark-talk-architecture
evals.prompt: Je fais un talk sur notre archi événementielle avec des slides en dark mode : services commandes, paiement et stock publient sur Kafka, un service de notifications consomme. Fais-moi le schéma Excalidraw qui va bien.
evals.expected_output: The night style: dark canvas, light text, one accent on Kafka or the flow that matters, French text kept as given, lint clean with no contrast warnings.
expectations: The canvas background is dark (luminance below 0.2)
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors and no contrast warnings
Kafka appears between the publishing services and the notification service

evals.name: flashcards-deck
evals.prompt: Make me a small deck of flashcards, like a pocket guide, to teach our new developers three code review habits: small merge requests, explain the why in the description, and run the tests before asking for review. Portrait cards I can post one by one.
evals.expected_output: A cover with the three habits listed, then one portrait card per habit (poster title, short text, one small diagram, a rule-of-thumb box), each exportable alone at 4:5, lint clean.
expectations: The scene contains 4 portrait cards of equal size with a 4:5 ratio (cover + 3)
The cover lists the three habits in a numbered table of contents
Each concept card has exactly one title, one small diagram and one rule-of-thumb box
lint_scene.py reports 0 errors
A per-card export command or PNG at 1200 x 1500 is provided
